pageTitle: CircuitLab AI · From faults to evidence
description: An electronic diagnosis assistant connecting hypotheses, measurements and verification. Discover CircuitLab AI and enter your laboratory.
eyebrow: YOUR CIRCUIT HAS SOMETHING TO SAY
heroBody: CircuitLab AI connects what you observe with what you can measure. An assistant for investigating electronic faults, testing hypotheses and checking every repair.
heroNote: Made for learning, building and trying again.
illustration: Illustrative schematic of a 5 V voltage divider with two 10 kilohm resistors and a measurement point at the output.
evidenceBody: The objective, photos and a confirmed schematic form the starting point. Hidden connections require human confirmation.
measureBody: The assistant proposes what to check at an allowed point. Every reading keeps its source: manual, instrumented or simulated.
verifyBody: A person performs the repair. New readings are compared with the functional criteria defined before diagnosis.
exampleNote: This schematic and its values explain the workflow; they do not represent a real measurement.
howTitle: From “it doesn't work” to a concrete test.
howBody: Every step leaves a clearer question and a record you can review. A diagnosis can finish resolved or inconclusive.
stepOneBody: Explain what the circuit should do and what is happening. Attach photos and confirm its connections.
stepTwoBody: Review possible causes and the evidence for or against them. The assistant proposes a check to tell them apart.
stepThreeBody: Record a manual reading or use a bridge at instrumented points. You confirm the conditions and make the physical change.
stepFourBody: Compare new readings against the original criterion. Export a report with hypotheses, sources and a timeline.
detailTitle: You can review how each conclusion was reached.
detailBody: Photos, confirmed connections, hypotheses and measurements belong to the same session. Visual observations and electrical readings retain their context.
detailFour: Readable reports and exportable JSON data
traceOneBody: Connections and points recorded by a person.
traceTwoBody: The point, conditions and source of the reading.
traceThreeBody: The change stays in the timeline.
traceFourBody: The numerical criterion is evaluated without asking the model for an opinion.
circuitsTitle: Three families. Plenty of useful questions.
circuitsBody: The prototype focuses on low-voltage educational setups with confirmed schematics and test points.
ledBody: Connect the observed behavior with the power supply, confirmed connections and measurements in your setup.
dividerBody: Compare the output voltage with the expected range and document the checks you performed.
sensorBody: Investigate unexpected readings and check voltages at previously instrumented points.
circuitsNote: The initial catalog does not cover arbitrary circuits or multiple simultaneous faults.
scopeTitle: Learn with the circuit in front of you.
scopeBody: For students, educators and prototyping teams who want to investigate a setup and keep a reviewable explanation of their tests.
scopeOneTitle: Android at the bench. Web for review.
scopeOneBody: Capture evidence on your phone and review sessions, hypotheses and reports on a larger screen.
scopeTwoBody: The interface, reports and new diagnoses support both languages. Human-entered data retains its original language.
scopeThreeBody: The AI integration uses Meta Model API when configured. Validation with the real model and real hardware remains part of the work ahead.
faqOneQ: Do I need hardware to try it?
faqOneA: You can explore the system in simulation mode, clearly identified in the application. That mode tests the workflow without performing an AI diagnosis or establishing physical measurements. For a real circuit, record manual readings or configure a bridge and a calibrated board.
faqTwoQ: Can the AI repair the circuit for me?
faqTwoA: A person carries out physical interventions. The assistant proposes checks and changes, but requires human confirmation. A photo does not establish electrical continuity or hidden connections.
faqThreeA: The initial scope covers an LED with resistor, a voltage divider and an analog sensor within the documented 0–5 V limits. Points and conditions are confirmed before measuring. Mains electricity, medical devices and arbitrary circuit repairs are outside the scope.
faqFourQ: How do I access the laboratory?
faqFourA: Sign in with an account created by your installation's administrator. The sign-in page lets you choose English or Spanish. Analysis needs a connection to the API; using Meta requires provider credentials configured on the server.
closingTitle: Give every repair a way to be verified.
closingBody: Open a session, define what you expect from the circuit and start gathering evidence.
